title: Introduce credential prefab and stream.slice adapters; unify retry presets and bump SDK versions
author: Elena Morales
description: Motivation: SDK consumers repeatedly requested a lightweight, cross-language credential 'prefab' that can be used for local testing, session-less calls, and as a deterministic fallback when the full credential orchestration is unavailable. Separately, several teams ran into ergonomic friction when consuming long streaming payloads and manually slicing token/byte windows; we introduce a small stream.slice helper to provide safe, backpressure-aware slicing across SDKs. This PR implements: 1) credential-prefab: a minimal, serializable credential object present in Python/TS/Go SDKs that implements the same surface as live credentials but with no background refresh or heartbeat; 2) stream.slice adapters: ergonomic helpers on top of the existing async iterator/pullstream primitives to request deterministic fixed-size slices with optional overlap and retry predicates; 3) resilience preset consolidation: add a new retry profile "resilience-light" and align default retry ceilings across SDKs to avoid surprising crosslang behavior; 4) coordinated SDK bumps: py-sdk 1.30.0, ts-sdk 1.29.3, go-sdk v1.9.0. Checklist: - [x] design doc (ENG-1832) reviewed - [x] unit tests for prefab and slice helpers - [x] integration tests exercising prefab fallback path with no credential service - [x] docs updated (examples and CHANGELOGs) - [x] release notes drafted Related: ENG-1899 (stream ergonomics), SUP-452 (support ticket referencing flaky streaming during credential rotation). Implementation notes: credential-prefab is explicitly opt-in and cannot be used where HSM/KMS-backed keys are required; it exposes an is_live flag and a small metadata map to keep parity with the full credential type. stream.slice is implemented as a thin adapter: it consumes the upstream async iterator, yields slice objects with start/end offsets and idempotency tokens, and obeys SDK-level cancellation signals. To avoid hidden regressions we preserved existing stream contracts and added explicit telemetry hooks for slice start/finish. Migration: no forced migration required; consumers opt-in to prefab via Cred.prefab(...) factory and call stream.slice(...) when they want deterministic slicing. Rollout: feature flagged on the server for telemetry gating for 2 weeks before we recommend general use.

review_comments: Sven Fischer: Looks good overall. Two nits: (1) can we keep the telemetry event name shorter (slice.start -> stream.slice_start)?; (2) prefer an explicit error when prefab is used in an environment marked 'requires_kms' rather than a silent no-op.

Elena Morales (author): Addressed both in the latest commit. Renamed the telemetry event and added a runtime check that throws a clear error when prefab is instantiated in a restricted environment. See commit feat(auth): refuse prefab in requires_kms env.
Nina Gomez: Tests are thorough. Please add one more unit test to ensure stream.slice respects cancellation during backoff. Also confirm docs mention the opt-in nature of prefab for compliance teams.
Elena Morales: Added cancellation test and expanded docs with a compliance note. Also added a short example showing a graceful fallback to prefab in the Python example.
Ravi Sharma: CI flakes on Go windows build — looks related to a flaky temp file cleanup in slice_adapter test. Recommend adding deterministic temp dir usage.
Elena Morales: Fixed the Go test to use t.TempDir() and re-ran CI. All green now.
release_notes: Python SDK 1.30.0: add credential-prefab and stream.slice helper; examples and CHANGELOG updated
TypeScript SDK 1.29.3: add credential-prefab, stream.slice, and resilience-light retry preset
Go SDK v1.9.0: add credential-prefab and slice adapter; minor API parity improvements
Note: credential-prefab is opt-in and must not be used in KMS/HSM-required deployments
